Read `GameEngine.swift` in full to verify it against what I wrote blind two rounds ago in `GameView`/`GameBoardView` — and caught something urgent along the way.

- **Do NOT delete `Domain/RestoreIntegrityService.swift` — that would break the build Claude B is trying to protect.** Claude B's suggestion (made this same round) was reasoning from "GameEngine doesn't exist yet, so nothing depends on the bare name." But Codex A's brand-new `GameEngine.swift` line 37 is `integrity: RestoreIntegrityService = .init()` — it depends on the bare `RestoreIntegrityService` name directly, via that exact deprecated typealias. Both were written in the same parallel round without either seeing the other's file. Deleting it next turn would trade a cosmetic deprecation warning for a real "cannot find type" break. The actually-correct cleanup (for whenever someone touches `Domain/GameEngine.swift` anyway) is changing that one init parameter to `DomainPersistenceRestoreIntegrityService`, then deleting the typealias file — not deleting the file first.
- **Real, confirmed functional bug in my own `SettingsView.swift` from last round, now fixable:** it persists `drawMode`/`timerEnabled` straight to `SettingsStore` via my own `SettingsViewModel`, completely bypassing `GameEngine.setDrawMode(_:)` — which now exists and contains the *required* "finalize active session as a loss, then deal fresh in the new mode" logic (matches `DEC-app_features-005`). Right now, changing draw mode in Settings would silently write a file the live `GameEngine` instance never re-reads, while the actual running game keeps playing in the old mode. Next turn I need to route draw-mode changes through `engine.setDrawMode(mode)` instead, and replace my hardcoded `hasActiveGame: true` placeholder with the real `engine.state.terminalState == .active`, now that `GameEngine` exists to read it from.
- **Related gap this exposes in `GameEngine` itself:** there's no public `setTimerEnabled(_:)` mirroring `setDrawMode(_:)` — `settings.timerEnabled` is loaded once at bootstrap and private, so even after I fix the draw-mode routing, toggling "Show Timer" in Settings still has no way to affect the live session this run. Worth Codex A adding a small public setter the same shape as `setDrawMode`.
- **Codex B's own suggested integrator wiring snippet won't compile as described:** it says call `engine.freezeTimer()` then `gameSaveStore.flush()` — but `GameEngine` has no public `freezeTimer()` (only `private func freezeTimerClock()`). `GameEngine.flushPersistence()` (already public) already does freeze-then-flush-all-three-stores internally in the correct order — the actual correct scenePhase-background wiring is just `await engine.flushPersistence()`, no separate `SceneLifecycleCoordinator` orchestration needed for this integration point.
- **Good news, worth saying plainly:** `GameEngine`'s real public surface (`state`, `interaction`, `selectCard(pile:index:)`, `attemptMove(to:)`, `drawFromStock()`, `undo()`, `newGame(drawMode:requiresConfirmation:)`) matches exactly what `GameView`/`GameBoardView` bet on two rounds ago, including same-card-retap-to-deselect and a source pile correctly excluded from its own `legalDestinations` — traced it by hand and found no mismatch.
